notes: Code-blind review of production input sequence. The rider and saddle read clearly on land. Sampled frames establish a static silhouette and missing surface cues; motion timing needs continuous review. Distinct from P2-071 human swimming pose.

subject: Aquaryn dismount camera obstruction
defect: After dismount the camera sits close behind Aquaryn so its back and fins fill much of the view and obscure the trainer and shore-return action
notes: The empty saddle proves a dismount state but these frames cannot show whether the trainer swims or reaches land. Confirm camera recovery in continuous ordinary play; this fixture may keep the mount unusually close.

subject: Hollows fight loss result clarity
defect: After the creature falls a large out-of-fight message appears over the exploration HUD while TEAM 5/5 and green party bars still look ready and no distinct loss result is shown
notes: Code-blind 65-second normal-input named-wild fight. At i13 Sparkit has an empty bar and KO tag; at 99-after the ordinary green roster returns beside duplicate out-of-fight text. This is a loss sequence, not a victory. The legal level-42 fixture fought one named wild; confirm normal campaign party recovery semantics before selecting a fix.

subject: Hollows victory reward tiles
defect: The win panel shows one small blue reward icon with x1 beside four unlabeled white plus tiles so the earned item and unused slots are difficult to distinguish
notes: Code-blind review of natural Hollows victory with legal five-creature level-80 capture party. Cyan victory text and +638 XP are clear; a broad reward panel obscures most of the visibly collapsed Voltarach. Inspect cleared-panel aftermath separately. One second after the first result shot, the reward panel still covers much of the recovered creature/body area; the defeated body is only a tangle of blue legs behind Sparkit and the overlay, so fainted silhouette and ground contact cannot be judged independently.

subject: captain fight camera orientation
defect: During incoming warnings the camera repeatedly faces an empty part of the arena or crops the opponent and ally so the attack direction and exchange are difficult to read
notes: Deferred to Cloudreach gameplay/Claude camera owner: the live-input captain-fight evidence shows framing loss, but camera logic is excluded by CODEX_START_HERE section2c. Preserve the original manifest repro for the gameplay camera pass. Original evidence: Code-blind review of full three-opponent live-input Captain Veyra fight. Aeriex and Cloudfang leave the frame during incoming cues; a later reverse angle cuts off Cloudfang head and much of Sparkit. Distinct from Meadows P2-062 where the nearby ally fills and clips the view. The challenge and victory callbacks succeeded.

subject: catch camera distance
defect: Catch framing crowds the trainer and both creatures during aim then jumps close enough at strike and breakout to crop bodies and lose the orb path
notes: Code-blind review of complete dry First Shore wild catch sequence. Cannonback, Terrapup and trainer overlap at aim distance; impact circle dominates Cannonback. The catch failure and success states are genuine pinned rolls, but a second same-species body may be in the scene. Stormwood Voltwig/Terrapup capture repeats the tight overlap and cropped strike; the dark ground makes the chance text more legible than Tidewake. Cloudreach repeats this with trainer across Skyrill face, a second body behind, then tight overhead contact. Code-blind review.

subject: catch chance HUD contrast
defect: The capture chance label and percentage sit over the trainer and pale grass with weak contrast, making the changing odds difficult to scan while aiming
notes: The 4% to 41% values are visible on inspection, while the CAPTURE CHANCE label nearly disappears into the background. Assess on the actual 1920x1080 display before choosing a panel or text treatment. Cloudreach chance text crosses character models and pale sky with similarly weak contrast.

subject: authored camp creature bed silhouette
defect: The creature bed reads as a flat brown patch inside a dark oval curb and becomes a narrow ring when seen edge-on, with little bedding shape to identify it as a resting place
notes: Code-blind review of three authored camp fixtures from the normal player camera. Camp tent and fire are clearly identifiable; no sleep interaction was performed. Salt Crown is most edge-on, so confirm alternate approach before assigning every weak read to the mesh.

subject: authored camp workbench identity
defect: The craft station looks like a narrow plain wooden bench with no obvious tools or work surface cues, and in two camp views it is partly hidden by the trainer
notes: Code-blind normal-camera review at three authored camps. This is the world station, distinct from CraftPanel text issues P2-095 and P2-096. At First Shore the fixture player appears to stand on the bench; confirm a natural approach before attributing that placement to gameplay.

subject: catch chance feedback timing
defect: A stale failed-catch message remains along the bottom while the new aim state shows 100% CAPTURE CHANCE and a nearly empty target bar
notes: Code-blind still-frame finding: bottom says not even close — weaken it first after the target has been weakened. Confirm duration in motion before choosing an update trigger.

subject: full-party catch choice legibility
defect: The full-party caught-creature choice panel leaves the earlier battle HUD visible through its transparent background and puts dim choice instructions at the screen bottom
notes: Code-blind normal 1920x1080 capture. Full party is fixture context; this scores only overlapping layers and faint instructions. Selection mechanics are not inferred.

subject: Fly carrier grip pose
defect: The trainer hangs rigidly upright beneath Galecrest with raised straight arms and dangling legs, so the bird reads as perched on the hands rather than carrying a person
notes: Code-blind comparison across three production-camera flight sequences. Meadows launch was reshot with a settled camera and clearly repeats the pose. The carrier silhouette is strong, but the body hold is unconvincing. Stormwood disclosed canopy fixture repeats the same hold; it does not establish campaign reachability.
